Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list; happy to outline how this works at a high level and next steps for an export. TL;DR: hosted defaults are conservative, exports are supported via Console + API, and region metadata is preserved. Details below.

Retention (hosted customers, default tiers):
- Access logs (HTTP/connection-level): 90 days default.
- Audit/event logs (configuration changes, token activity, role grants): 365 days default.
- Admin/user action logs (console actions, role changes, manual exports): 365 days.

Export capabilities:
- Exports can be run from the Redwood Console (Admin > Logs > Export) or programmatically via the Logs Export API.
- Supported archive formats: NDJSON (recommended for fidelity), CSV (field-flattened view), and gzipped bundles for large ranges.
- You can request a single archive covering 1+ month ranges — we will chunk server-side into multi-part archives when size > 10GB, but provide a single manifest and presigned S3 links.

Region mapping and residency:
- Logs are written in the region where the request completed. Each event contains a region tag (region: us-west-2 / eu-central-1 etc.). Exports preserve that metadata.
- If your tenant is US-based but you have EU-origin requests, events created in EU will be stored in EU-backed storage and the export will include them with their region metadata. Exports do not automatically re-reside data unless you request a cross-region transfer (see below).

Deletion & legal hold:
- Standard deletion: customers can request individual-record deletion or dataset deletion via a support ticket. For hosted plans, deletion is performed within 7 business days after verification.
- Legal hold / extended retention: we can apply retention overrides (e.g., hold logs for 3+ years) for customers with an agreement. This is typically applied at the tenant or dataset level.

What to expect next / deliverables:
- I attached a short export guide (audit_export_instructions.pdf) that walks through Console and API steps and the manifest format.
- If you confirm the ranges in haven_log_request.csv we will: (1) validate that all ranges are within retention windows, (2) kick an export job and provide presigned S3 URLs, and (3) include a sample NDJSON export for your engineers to validate schema.

Notes & constraints:
- For hosted tenants with default retention, we cannot export data older than the retention window unless you purchased extended retention.
- Exports contain only the fields allowed by your role & policy; PII redaction can be applied on export upon request (may delay delivery by 24–48 hours).

I'll have Marcus scope the cross-region pieces below — looping him in.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — a few operational clarifications from infra/ops so you have the full picture:

1) Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private customers:
- Hosted (standard): retention defaults as Kimberly noted. Exports delivered as presigned S3 links hosted in the generating region.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): customers can configure retention up to 3 years via the admin console; exports follow the dedicated cluster's region setting.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed storage — full control over retention/export. We provide tooling and an offline export bundle if needed.

2) Export delivery & keys:
- Exports are uploaded to signed S3 buckets in the same region as the logs (or to a region you request for cross-region transfer). We provide one-time presigned URLs valid for 7 days by default.
- If you use a customer-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private, we can encrypt the export with your key (requires advance notice).

3) Metadata and filtering:
- Exports include: timestamp, event_type, user_id (hashed if redaction requested), tenant_id, region, resource_path, ip (optional/redacted), and raw_payload for audit events.
- Filtering: you can request filters (by region, event_type, user_id) at export time. Cross-region exports will include region tags so you can split after download if desired.

4) SLA & timeline:
- Export jobs for <=30 days: typical turnaround 24–48 hours. Larger or redaction/PII requests may take 72 hours+.
- Deletion requests: standard 7 business days after verification; emergency requests (compliance/legal) handled within 48 hours if escalation provided.

If you'd like a small NDJSON sample, I've generated a sanitized sample and uploaded it to the shared Drive link. Attaching the sample filename here: export_sample.ndjson.

Happy to schedule a 30-min call with your security team if there are any export formatting or retention-policy specifics to agree on.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Product Manager
